subject: Evidence handoff: preferred format, integrity checks and delivery window
messages:
From: Jane Park <jane.park@finacorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: AuditsOps <audits@finacorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@finacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence delivery: acceptable formats and timeline?

Hi Olga,

As part of our security review for the pilot account, our audit team needs a short note on how Redwood plans to deliver historical audit evidence if we request it during due diligence or an incident. Specifically: 

- Preferred export format(s) for audit logs and event streams (schema, compression).
- How you deliver integrity proofs (hashes, signed manifests).
- Typical lead time for an extract (SLA for a standard 30-day request and for a larger 6-month window).
- Whether you can deliver a chain-of-custody statement and whether exports can be sent to our S3 or only to a shared link.

Can you send a short, actionable response and a ballpark timeline for delivery? We may need the output as part of our contract appendix.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Director, Security Assurance
Finacorp Systems
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@finacorp.com>
Cc: AuditsOps <audits@finacorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@finacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence delivery: acceptable formats and timeline?

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. High level answer below; attaching a concise specification (evidence-package-spec.pdf) and a small sample bundle (sample-ndjson.tar.gz) so your audit team can validate locally.

1) Export formats and schema
- Primary delivery: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) files, partitioned by service/component and day, compressed with gzip. Each record contains an ISO-8601 timestamp, event_type, request_id, user_id (redacted if required), model_id, route, and a payload object for request/response metadata.
- Alternative: Parquet (columnar) export for large bulk analytics on request.
- Small exports (<10GB) can be delivered as a single tar.gz; large exports are delivered as a manifest referencing S3 prefixes.

2) Integrity and verification
- We compute SHA-256 checksums for each file and provide a signed manifest (metadata + checksums). We can GPG-sign the manifest using our key and include the public key fingerprint in the chain-of-custody. Checksums are included in sha256-checksums.txt (see attached sample).
- Optional: timestamped notarization via an external TSP for forensic needs (additional cost/time).

3) Delivery options and lead times
- Direct delivery options: secure pre-authenticated S3 write to your bucket (preferred), SFTP to an agreed host, or temporary HTTPS download from our hardened transfer service.
- SLA guidance (ballpark):
  - Standard 30-day window (up to 30 days of events): typical turnaround 3–5 business days from signed request and authorization.
  - Medium export (31–180 days): typical turnaround 5–10 business days.
  - Large exports (>180 days or >2TB): we schedule with capacity planning; typical 10–20 business days depending on scope and retention tiering.
- Expedited processing available (24–48 hours) for high-priority incident response with an associated expedited fee.

4) Chain-of-custody and evidence artifacts
- We provide: signed manifest, per-file checksums, export job logs (who requested/exported), time-synchronized server timestamps, and an export job report (CSV) summarizing counts and byte sizes.
- Chain-of-custody statement: we issue a short affidavit describing custody handoff, export method, responsible engineer, and storage location.

5) Retention windows and snapshots
- Audit logs are retained per customer-configurable retention policies. Our default hosted retention is 90 days for request/response traces and 365 days for high-fidelity audit streams (configurable via contract). Long-term archival to cold storage can be provided for multi-year retention.

Notes and next steps
- Attached spec contains field-level descriptions and a sample NDJSON payload.
- If you prefer delivery to your S3, please share a write-only bucket ARN and a minimal IAM policy we can use; we'll provide a test manifest before final delivery.

CCing Marissa for contract appendix language and Karthik for technical acceptance tests.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-package-spec.pdf, sample-ndjson.tar.gz, sha256-checksums.txt

- Karthik: technical acceptance — can you review attachment and confirm our NDJSON schema and delivery tooling (S3 write role) are accurate? Any constraints that would affect lead times?
- Ben: ops intake — estimate internal effort to support a 6-month export (~0.5–1.0 FTE for coordination + infra I/O pricing). Also confirm we can provide a GPG-signed manifest and whether timestamping via TSP is supported out-of-the-box.

Thanks — this is very helpful and exactly what our auditors asked for. A couple quick clarifications before we finalize the appendix: 

- Can you confirm whether internal request logs include the full request payload or if PII is redacted by default? We need a statement for the appendix.
- For S3 direct delivery, our security team prefers a write-only role with forced TLS and access logging enabled; we'll send a template policy.

If you can confirm those two items, we can proceed to insert the language into our procurement docs. Also please share the Drive folder link with the sample bundle when convenient (you already attached the files; our team will validate).
